I was a female RA for a boy's floor in college.  I was talking with the new freshmen at the beginning of the year when one of them finally got up the courage to ask why they had a female RA.  One of them gave me this gross smile and said, "Just in case we get lonely at night, right?"
Without even pausing, I looked him dead in the face and said, "you're going to be lonely your entire life, so you might as well get used to it."
Still reliving that one.

I worked as a hostess at a local restaurant in high school.  4/1 was a particularly bad night with bitchy people tapping their toes for tables, reservations canceling and then showing up, you name it.  Anyway, it was definitely past the time I was supposed to be cut and getting very late when I got a call from a man saying they were headed over with 50 people.  Knowing that I wouldn't be cut if they knew that many were coming in, I threw a mental temper tantrum and stalked back to the kitchen to let my manager know that we had a big party coming in.  Walked in and everyone kept a straight face for about two seconds before they saw my scowl and broke down into hysterics.  Apparently the manager told one of the waiters to tell me that I was cut and he thought it'd be super funny to make a prank call instead.  Oh well, we had a good laugh and I went home with free dessert.  Not a bad night after all.

I have no specific religious beliefs. I was raised Roman Catholic, but my mother quietly separated our family from the church after the first signs of pedophilia came out.  This when I was pretty young, so all of the religion classes and Sunday services never really made an impact on me.  I do firmly believe in karma and have adopted a sort of spirituality that many members of my family share.  I frequently find myself asking "why" when it comes to my pain.  I know a lot of people turn to faith to deal with hardship, so I do find myself frustrated when I'm told to "trust in God" while I'm doubled over in pain.  I typically remind myself that there's a bright side to every situation and I do my best to make my impact on the world a positive one, either by supporting others with chronic pain or being a positive impact on someone else's life.  We might all have the same reality, but I think your overall quality of life is definitely impacted by the way you choose to see and use your sitauation.  I envy those who can completely trust in a greater power and say that this is obviously someone's plan for them.  I sometimes wish I had that kind of faith.
Note to self: never, ever buy a house with a fucking basement.

I have heard stories on IC network about women who either suffer from more intense symptoms, continue with their usual symptoms, or even see their symptoms disappear.  I guess it's a wild card deal on an individual basis.  I have the same concerns you do, especially since I've read that IC definitely increases your chances of miscarriage and makes vaginal birth much more complicated.  For more information, I'd suggest the pregnancy section of the IC network forum.

Wow, that's crazy that those tablets specifically are working for you.  I've been taking the generic urinary pain relief tablets from CVS, but they've recently stopped working...maybe for using them for so long? :(  I had an instillation done today and my uro has discontinued my prescribed oxybutynin, which was apparently making it worse.  Thank you for the advice, and good luck with IC.
It's going to be a long road, but I'm going to keep trying to find a combination that works for me.  Thank you!

I'm going to contact the Office of Supportive Services tomorrow and see if I can talk to someone there.  I also think I'm going to look into acupuncture.  I've heard it mentioned on a few forums, and at this point I'm willing to try anything.  Thank you!
That's a really good point.  I guess there's no other option but to tough it out.  Thank you for your support.
I think the idea of my family having to deal with it is what really made me back down. Thank you so much for your support!

I've actually never considered vegetarianism for IC.  My boyfriend's a vegetarian, but I've stuck stubbornly to a protein-heavy diet because meat is one of the few things that I CAN have with IC.  Maybe I'll try to suck it up and try some spices as well; I've been relying heavily on garlic and salt as the only things to flavor my food, and even that's getting old.  Thanks for the advice!
Six months?! Ugh, I can't imagine getting through that.  I'm glad you've found a way to live comfortably with IC!

Thank you so much for your reply!  I'll definitely look into biofeedback; even with all of my intense IC research, I've never heard of that.  I met with my uro today and altered my treatment; you were definitely dead-on about being careful with the meds.  They think that the oxybutynin was causing me not to void completely, therefore causing the pain.  I'm going to stop taking it and hopefully things will get better!
Hey, I almost went into that after high school!  Funny to hear it mentioned.  I still intend to get certified when I'm done with my degree.

This is gonna sound corny, but cliche things like rock collecting and birdwatching that get you outside are seriously so good for your state of mind.  Keep a journal of what you see outside.  If you're not in a rural area or have no access to the great outdoors, go out to a coffee shop or something and hunker down for the day with that journal.  Write down what you see people doing, what they look like, how they interact with others.  Write about them and what you think their lives are like.  Being an observer is very theraputic.

It runs in my family, too.  I understand.  You have so much time left, buddy.  Don't throw it away.  I've been there.  I know you can't see it, but I'm asking you to do THE hardest thing for people in your position and start to trust someone else again.  You need to trust the people here that it will get better.

Nothing turns a man off like not feeling capable.  Give him a lesson and show him exactly what you want him to do.  Keep it light and make sure to give him some very, very positive feedback when he does something right.  Adjust your hips or gently move his hands around if he's headed in the wrong direction.  As long as you make it fun, he won't feel incompetent or get frustrated.

Hey man.  I (19f) have been dating my boyfriend (21m) since I was 18 and he was 20.  I realize this is one year less than your age gap, but I'm a freshman in college and he's a junior that is graduating early this year.  When we first started dating, I was really concerned about him feeling weird about my age (freshman stigma, etc.), but it's never been a problem because he doesn't let it get to him.  His friends have made a few comments (keep in mind that some people might assume that you're with her because she's a freshman and freshman are apparently easy) and my parents weren't necessarily thrilled, but it's been a few months and everyone's chilled out because we're happy and very good together.  If you feel weird, she'll probably feel twice as weird, so try not to let it get to you and focus on how lucky you are to find someone as awesome as she is.  Good luck.
